 Judgment

The appeal is filed by the Insurance Company calling in question the judgment and award dated 10.02.2011, in M.V.C. No.1112/2005, passed by the learned I Additional Senior Civil Judge & Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belgaum, on the ground that the claimant was gratuitous passenger in the Tempo Trax goods vehicle.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.

2. On 20.09.2004 at about 1.30 p.m. the claimant was traveling in the Tempo Trax bearing registration No.KA-22/8988 from Belgaum to Khanapur as an occupant in the said Tempo Trax and when they reached near Shivaji Statue at Peeranwadi on Belgaum-Khanapur Road, a Truck bearing registration No.KA-22/B-4142 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Tempo Trax resulting which the driver of the Tempo Trax and claimant have sustained injuries.
The Tribunal held that the both drivers of Truck and Tempo Trax are equally responsible for the accident due to their rash and negligent driving.
4. The appellant-Insurance Company is the insurer of Tempo Trax bearing registration No.KA.22/8988.
It is the contention urged by the appellant that the vehicle is Tempo Trax goods vehicle and the claimant has travelled in the said vehicle as gratuitous passenger.

Therefore,
Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation.
5. Admittedly, in the present case, the Tempo Trax is a goods vehicle.

From the complaint averment,
Ex.P.1 itself revealed that the claimant has travelled in the Tempo Trax besides sitting to the driver.
The claimant in his evidence in the course of the cross-examination has admitted that his employer is one Atul Bhavasar and he is working in Techno Filters Pvt. Ltd. from 15 years.
Therefore, it is proved that the claimant is not a cleaner in the Tempo Trax and has not travelled in the said Tempo Trax as an authorized representative of goods or owner of the goods.

Therefore, when from the evidence of the NC: 2023:KHC-D:9033 claimant-PW.1 itself proved that he was working in some other company under different employer and therefore, he is not an employee in the Tempo Trax.
Hence, it is proved that the claimant has travelled in the said Tempo Trax as an unauthorized passenger.
But the Tempo Trax is a goods vehicle.
Therefore, it is proved that the claimant is a gratuitous passenger.
Hence, Tempo Trax is used for the purpose other than permitted.

Hence,
there is violation of conditions of insurance policy.
Therefore, the Insurance Company of the Tempo Trax is not liable to indemnify the owner and to pay the compensation.
Hence, respondent No.4 is liable to pay compensation to the claimant.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:

3 ORDER i) The appeal is allowed.
 ii) The judgment and order dated  10.02.2011, in M.V.C. No.1112/2005,
passed by the learned I Additional Senior Civil Judge & Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belgaum is modified to the NC: 2023:KHC-D:9033 extent that the appellant-Insurance Company is exonerated from the payment of compensation.
 iii) Respondent No.4 is directed to pay  compensation to the claimant with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
